norms.what: A stage skill is model-invocable so the orchestrator can start it, which also lets Claude invoke it on an unrelated task; the run-file guard makes that cost one skill load. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).
After compaction the orchestrator, the oldest skill of the run, is the first to be dropped; re-invoking it restores the run's standing rules. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).

Each trap records the passage it rests on and the date it was verified; comparing them with the page as it reads today keeps a trap from outliving the docs (#34). The raw page is needed, since a paraphrase cannot confirm a verbatim passage. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).

A comparison made by commands gives the same verdict on every run and keeps the pages out of context. The normalisation is the one the knowledge files' passages were verified with: on 2026-09-29 these commands found all 95 recorded passages, and reported `changed` for a planted, altered one. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).

A changed passage does not prove the trap wrong, so the trap still runs, capped and flagged, and the user sees what the page says now; only a passage that holds counts as re-verified. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).
System cards are PDFs; without a text converter their passages cannot be compared, and saying so is better than a guess. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).
A knowledge file is the maintainers' record, re-verified in a reviewed change; a run that rewrote it would hide the drift it found. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).
One line per source lets the traps stage cap stale traps and the report show them, with the text the page holds today. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #43).
